section spaces are finite-dimensional.  No cover hypothesis, no χ, no exactness datum: it is
`sectionSub k ⊤ D ≤ sectionSub k U₀ D` (antitonicity in the open) composed with the freeze.

**This is the root cause of everything in §5–§6, and it is worth stating separately because it is
stronger and simpler than the χ-level statements.**  Riemann–Roch says `ℓ(D)` grows like
`deg D`; this says it *cannot*, along any tower at a point missing a chart whose sections are
finite-dimensional.  So `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)` at a **non-total** `U` is not
bookkeeping — it is a substantive geometric restriction, and any theorem assuming it over all
divisors has already excluded the curves Riemann–Roch is about.

Consequence for reading this whole module: the `[∀ D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k Uᵢ D)]`
binders on §5–§6 are what make the refutations available, and a consumer who supplies them for
convenience has chosen the geometry.  Found by a fresh-context review of this module. -/
theorem ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ : X.Opens)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] (n : ℕ) :
    ell k (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ E) := by
  have hsub : sectionSub k ⊤ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ sectionSub k U₀ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E) :=
    sectionSub_antitone_open k le_top _
  rw [sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem k U₀ hP E n] at hsub
  exact Submodule.finrank_mono hsub

/-- **`hbump` IS FALSE whenever some prime divisor sits off one chart of the cover.**

Unconditional: no `chi_add`, no exactness hypothesis, no approximation input.  `hbump` forces
`χ` to grow linearly along the tower `n·P` while `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` bounds it,
so `hbump` cannot hold.

**This is inbox `I-0449`'s conclusion, strengthened.**  That audit derived the same
incompatibility *conditionally*, from `ChiLedger.chi_add`'s conclusion; an earlier version of
this module claimed on that basis that the audit had measured `chi_add` rather than `hbump`.
The claim was false and is retracted here in Lean rather than only in prose.

Note the reach: `P.point ∉ U₀` (or symmetrically `∉ U₁`) is far weaker than `P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`,
so this refutes `hbump` on a *larger* set of primes than `I-0449` addressed.  Together with
`LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump` — which derives the closed ledger *from* `hbump` — the honest
consequence is that the bump route to the ledger is dead for any cover having such a prime,
and consumers must not be pointed at it. -/
theorem not_bump_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)

    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]

19	  `relPicDeg_relPicMk : relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L`;

**There is no cheap honest route to `degree`. All three targets are blocked, and one of them is blocked by a signature bug rather than by mathematics.** Below, everything is verified by reading the cited lines; where I checked with the LSP I say so.

### The signature bug — read this first

`degree` cannot be written at its current type, for a reason independent of any missing mathematics. Its argument is a *bare scheme morphism*:

```lean
(Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) → ℤ
```

but `PicScheme.representable C` (`AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:576`) is a `Functor.RepresentableBy` in `Over (Spec (.of k))`, so its `homEquiv` consumes a morphism `T ⟶ PicScheme C` **in the over-category**. I probed this with the LSP at `IdentityComponent.lean:1432`: applying `homEquiv` to `lambda` fails with

```
Application type mismatch: The argument lambda has type
  Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left
but is expected to have type  ?m.50 ⟶ PicScheme C
```

To use `homEquiv` you must build `Over.homMk lambda h` with `h : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))` — and that fact is *not derivable* from a bare morphism (a `Spec k`-point of the underlying scheme need not be a `k`-point of the `k`-scheme; it could sit over a different `Spec k`-structure). I confirmed the `Over.homMk` route elaborates cleanly once that equation is supplied as `sorry`.

**Consequence:** at its current signature `degree` is *only* fillable by a junk constant, and `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` (which quantifies over the same bare-morphism type) is then false or vacuous. The honest first move is to fix the type — either take the argument in `Over (Spec (.of k))`, or carry the section equation as a hypothesis. This is cheap, it is in your lane (`IdentityComponent.lean`), and it must happen before any mathematics is worth doing.

### 1. What a k-point gives you: answer (b), a quotient with no canonical sheaf

Chasing the interface: `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean:150`), and `relPresheaf` (`RelPicFunctor.lean:855`) has object part

```
Quotient (relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
```

So `homEquiv` at `T = Spec k` lands in `Quotient (relPicSetoid C.hom (𝟙 _))`, where (`RelPicFunctor.lean:324`, `:394`) the setoid is the H_T-coset relation on `LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom πT` — and `OnProduct` (`Picard/LineBundlePullback.lean:136`) is

```lean
{ M : (Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules // IsLocallyTrivial M }
```

a genuine invertible sheaf on the categorical pullback `C ×_k Spec k`. So it is **(b) with a caveat that makes it nearly (a)**: an element is a quotient class, no canonical representative, but `Quotient.out` extracts one (noncomputably — fine, `degree` is already `noncomputable`; I verified `Quotient.out` + `out_eq` work).

The caveat that matters: at `T = Spec k` the H_T-subgroup ought to be trivial, because `Spec k` is a one-point space so every locally trivial sheaf on it is trivial — which would make the quotient *just* `Pic(C ×_k Spec k)` and representative-independence free. **That brick does not exist in the main project.** I searched: `IsLocallyTrivial` has exactly two lemmas about it in `LineBundlePullback.lean` (the definition :121 and `.pullback` :162), and there is no `Subsingleton`/one-point triviality lemma anywhere. The project has already audited this exact question and written the negative down. `Picard/DivDegree.lean:104-125`:

> the χ-ledger (`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic `RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree **cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic line bundle** `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)` regular-section bricks, also P3).

That is not a session; it is a campaign.

### 4. `finrank_eq_genus`: the bridge is missing infrastructure, and the statement is probably the wrong one

Given `Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom` and `dim_k T_0 = g`, mathlib **cannot** get you `topologicalKrullDim`. I checked exhaustively:

- `topologicalKrullDim` has essentially four lemmas in all of mathlib (`Mathlib/Topology/KrullDimension.lean:39-69`): monotone under inducing maps, invariant under homeomorphism, subspace bound, and `≤ 0` for discrete spaces. Plus `PrimeSpectrum.topologicalKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:1371`). Its only other appearances are in `AlgebraicGeometry/Artinian.lean`. **There is no `Scheme.dimension` in mathlib at all** and no lemma connecting `topologicalKrullDim` of a scheme to smoothness, relative dimension, or a tangent space.
- `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Smooth.lean:135`) is defined by *local standard-smooth presentations*, with no dimension-theoretic API — only composition, base change, and open immersions.
- The nearest bridge is `IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:76`): `finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R`. But `RegularLocalRing/` contains only `Defs.lean`, there is **no** "smooth over a field ⟹ regular local" instance anywhere (I grepped `IsRegularLocalRing` across all of mathlib — it appears only in its own defs file and `KrullDimension/Regular.lean`), and there is no `ringKrullDim = trdeg` for finite-type algebras. So even the local step is missing, before you get to gluing local ring dimension into `topologicalKrullDim` of the scheme.
- Neither project uses `topologicalKrullDim` anywhere except this one `sorry` (`IdentityComponent.lean:1474`).

**Also worth flagging:** the actual headline does not want this statement. `Jacobian.lean:357`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0`, needs `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Pic0Scheme C).hom` — not a Krull dimension. So `finrank_eq_genus` as stated is a *third* formulation, needing infrastructure nobody needs. I'd raise renaming or restating it as a question for the human before spending a session on it.

1. **Fix the `degree` signature** (over-category argument or a carried section hypothesis). Cheap, in your lane, and everything else is meaningless without it. Note that `kPoints_iff_kerDegree`'s `lambda` binder has the same defect.
2. **Build the one-point triviality brick**: a locally trivial sheaf on a scheme with subsingleton carrier is trivial, hence `relPicSetoid` at `T = Spec k` collapses to iso-classes. Small, self-contained, in `LineBundlePullback.lean`, and it is the thing that makes representative-independence free rather than a theorem. The Rebuild's analogue confirms the shape is right.
3. **Then** define `degree` via `hilbertPolynomial`'s leading coefficient on `Quotient.out` of the transported class. You would get a well-defined ℤ-valued function that is not provably the degree.

That last point is the crux, and it is why I think the answer to your question is a clean negative: **you can construct a total, well-defined `(Spec k ⟶ …) → ℤ` after steps 1–2, but you cannot prove it is the degree, and without that `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` is unreachable.** The two things that would change this — the `M ≅ O(div s)` regular-section bridge (campaign P3) and a cover on which the χ-ledger holds — are both campaign-sized, and the second is currently *refuted* for the covers on offer.

22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the multiplication isomorphism and class invariance
10	
11	This file supplies the **class-invariance layer** of the adelic χ-ledger: the
12	statement that all three numerical invariants of the ledger — `ℓ(D)`, `h¹(D)` and
13	`χ(D)` — depend only on the *linear-equivalence class* of `D`, together with the
14	elementary effective-witness dictionary that turns a nonzero global section into
15	an effective divisor in the same class.
16	
17	Everything here is **unconditional**: no gate class, no ledger exactness
18	hypothesis, no finiteness input.  The only mechanism is that multiplication by a
19	nonzero rational function `g ∈ K(X)^×` is a `k`-linear automorphism of `K(X)`
20	which carries the section subspace `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` *onto* `Γ(U, 𝒪(D − div g))`.
21	
22	## Main declarations
23	
24	* `Adelic.mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor` — the order computation
25	  `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f`, in section-membership form: the single
26	  arithmetic fact behind everything else in this file.
27	* `Adelic.mulEquivFunctionField` — multiplication by `g ≠ 0` as a `k`-linear
28	  automorphism of `K(X)` (`k` a field of constants).
29	* `Adelic.map_sectionSub_mulEquiv` — `(Γ(U, 𝒪(D))).map (g·) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`
30	  whenever `D'(P) = D(P) − ord_P g` for every prime divisor `P`.
31	* `Adelic.sectionSubMulEquiv` — the resulting `k`-linear isomorphism
32	  `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
33	* `Adelic.ell_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.h1dim_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_shift`
34	  — `ℓ`, `h¹` and `χ` are invariant under the shift `D ↦ D − div g`.
35	* `Adelic.chi_eq_of_principal_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`
36	  — the same statements spelled with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal` and with the
37	  project's `LinearEquivalence` relation.
38	* `Adelic.exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem` — the effective-witness
39	  brick: a nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` exhibits `D + div f ≥ 0` in the class of `D`.
40	* `Adelic.one_le_ell_of_nonneg` — conversely an effective divisor has `ℓ ≥ 1`.
41	
42	## Provenance
43	
44	The mathematical content is the adelic (function-field) incarnation of the
45	sibling project's sheaf-theoretic `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` /
46	`chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` pair
47	(`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, `RiemannRoch/MulEquiv.lean` and
48	`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`).  **No code was ported**: that development is built on
49	a different substrate (`CurveDivisor` on closed points, `divisorSheaf`,
50	`Sheaf.chi`, `CechPic`), none of whose names exist in this project.  What is
51	reused is the *argument*: transport `χ` along multiplication by `g` and cancel in
52	the ledger.  Here the transport is elementary linear algebra on subspaces of
53	`K(X)`, which is why this file needs no finiteness or exactness input at all —
54	whereas the sheaf-theoretic form needs the χ-additivity machinery even to state
55	the transport.
56	-/

58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	
60	universe u
61	
62	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
63	open scoped WithZero
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	namespace Adelic
67	
68	/-! ## §1. The order arithmetic behind the multiplication isomorphism -/
69	
70	section Order
71	
72	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
73	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
74	
75	/-- **Multiplication by `g` shifts the section bound by `div g`.**  If
76	`D'(P) ≥ D(P) − ord_P g` at every prime divisor `P` of `U`, then multiplication
77	by `g ≠ 0` carries `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` into `Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
78	
79	This is `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f` (`order_mul_of_ne_zero`) rearranged:
80	`ord_P (g·f) ≥ ord_P g − D(P) ≥ −D'(P)`.  Stated with an inequality rather than
81	an equality on `D'` so that the same lemma serves both directions of the
82	isomorphism (apply it to `g⁻¹` for the inverse). -/
83	theorem mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
84	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
85	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
86	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g ≤
87	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)
88	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D) :
89	    g * f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D' := by
90	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
91	  · simp
92	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
93	  have hord := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf P hP
94	  rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P hg hf0]
95	  have := hD' P hP
96	  linarith
97	
98	end Order
99	
100	/-! ## §2. Multiplication by `g` as a `k`-linear automorphism -/
101	
102	section MulEquiv
103	
104	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
105	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
106	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
107	
108	/-- **Multiplication by a nonzero rational function, as a `k`-linear
109	automorphism of `K(X)`.**  The inverse is multiplication by `g⁻¹`.  `k`-linearity
110	is automatic: multiplication by a fixed element of `K(X)` commutes with the
111	`k`-action. -/
112	noncomputable def mulEquivFunctionField (g : X.functionField) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
113	    X.functionField ≃ₗ[k] X.functionField :=
114	  LinearEquiv.ofLinear (LinearMap.mulLeft k g) (LinearMap.mulLeft k g⁻¹)
115	    (by ext x; simp [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hg])
116	    (by ext x; simp [inv_mul_cancel_left₀ hg])
117	
118	omit [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [X.IsRegularInCodimensionOne] [IsConstantField k X] in
119	@[simp] theorem mulEquivFunctionField_apply (g : X.functionField) (hg : g ≠ 0)
120	    (f : X.functionField) : mulEquivFunctionField k g hg f = g * f := rfl

Over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, every closed point of a smooth proper
curve `C` has residue field `k̄`, so each prime divisor `[P]` contributes degree
one to the sum, and `deg(D) := Σᵢ nᵢ` is the sum of the integer coefficients of
the formal sum `D = Σ nᵢ · [Pᵢ]`.

(Over a general field `k` one weights by the residue-field degrees
`Σᵢ nᵢ · [κ(Pᵢ) : k]` to recover the geometric degree; the project's RR bridge
needs only the `k̄` specialisation.)

Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_degree` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 137; Stacks 0BE0).

Implementation: `Finsupp.sum D (fun _ n => n)` is the sum of all coefficients of
the finitely supported function representing `D`. -/
noncomputable def degree (D : X.WeilDivisor) : ℤ :=
  (D : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ).sum (fun _ n => n)

/-- **The degree map is a group homomorphism `Div(C) → ℤ`.**

`deg(D₁ + D₂) = deg(D₁) + deg(D₂)`, `deg(-D) = -deg(D)`, `deg(0) = 0`. Bundled
as an `AddMonoidHom` for downstream use (the linear-equivalence quotient
`Cl(C) := Div(C) / im(div)` will inherit a `deg : Cl(C) → ℤ` from this).

Blueprint reference: `thm:divisor_degree_hom` (immediate from `def:divisor_degree`).

Implementation: built from `Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ)`, the
generic Mathlib packaging that lifts a family of `AddMonoidHom`s indexed by the
support into a single `AddMonoidHom` on the finsupp. Unfolds to
`D.sum (fun _ z ↦ z) = degree D` (see `degree_hom_apply` below). -/
noncomputable def degree_hom : X.WeilDivisor →+ ℤ :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ)

@[simp]
lemma degree_hom_apply (D : X.WeilDivisor) : degree_hom D = degree D :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom_apply (α := X.PrimeDivisor) (M := ℤ) (N := ℤ)
    (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ) D

/-- **Degree of the zero divisor is zero.** A direct consequence of
`degree_hom` being an `AddMonoidHom`. -/
@[simp]
lemma degree_zero : degree (0 : X.WeilDivisor) = 0 := by
  rw [← degree_hom_apply]; exact map_zero _

The proof (Hartshorne 6.10): if `f ∈ k̄` is constant then `div(f) = 0` and the
claim is trivial. Otherwise the inclusion `k̄(f) ⊂ K(C)` exhibits `K(C)` as a

finite morphism multiplies degree by `deg(φ)`. Two auxiliary sub-lemmas
(finite morphism induced by a non-constant rational function and multiplicativity
of degree under finite pullback) are the geometric inputs. -/

  -- this case split exactly recovers Hartshorne's constant-vs-non-constant
  -- split: `(∀ Y, ord_Y f = 0)` ⟺ `f ∈ k̄ \ {0}` (a nowhere-vanishing

  -- Hartshorne II.6.10's "if `f ∈ k̄` then `(f) = 0`").

* `IsRegularLocalRing` : A Noetherian local ring is regular if

* `IsRegularRing` : A noetherian ring is regular if its localization at any prime
  `IsRegularLocalRing`.

open IsLocalRing

/-- A Noetherian local ring is said to be regular if its maximal ideal
can be generated by `dim R` elements. -/
@[stacks 00KU]
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop extends
    IsLocalRing R, IsNoetherianRing R where
  spanFinrank_maximalIdeal : (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

lemma isRegularLocalRing_iff [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R :=
  ⟨fun ⟨h⟩ ↦ h, fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩⟩

namespace IsRegularLocalRing

lemma of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (le : (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank ≤ ringKrullDim R) : IsRegularLocalRing R :=
  (isRegularLocalRing_iff _).mpr (le_antisymm le (ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal R))

variable {R} in
lemma of_ringEquiv [IsRegularLocalRing R] {R' : Type*} [CommRing R']
    (e : R ≃+* R') : IsRegularLocalRing R' := by
  have := e.isLocalRing
  have := isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv R e
  rwa [isRegularLocalRing_iff, ← ringKrullDim_eq_of_ringEquiv e, ← map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal e,
    Ideal.spanFinrank_map_eq_of_ringEquiv, ← isRegularLocalRing_iff]

lemma iff_finrank_cotangentSpace [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R := by
  rw [isRegularLocalRing_iff, spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace]

instance [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] : IsRegularLocalRing R := by
  by_cases isf : IsField R
  · let := isf.toField
    simp [isRegularLocalRing_iff, maximalIdeal_eq_bot]
  · apply of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le
    rcases IsPrincipalIdealRing.principal (maximalIdeal R) with ⟨x, hx⟩
    simpa only [(IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one R) isf,
      Nat.cast_le_one, ← Set.ncard_singleton x, hx] using
        Submodule.spanFinrank_span_le_ncard_of_finite (Set.finite_singleton x)

end IsRegularLocalRing

/-- A noetherian ring is regular if its localization at any prime `IsRegularLocalRing`. -/
class IsRegularRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)

/-- **Pointed dual-number points of `X` at `e`, over `Spec k`.** The
`k[ε]`-valued points of `X` lying over the closed point of `Spec k[ε]` and
landing at `e`; the functor-of-points model of the Zariski tangent space at
`e`. A named restatement of the anonymous subtype
`overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual` targets, kept for readability
at the call sites below. -/
def pointedDualNumberPoints {k : Type u} [Field k] (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (e : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X.left) :=
  {g : Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X.left //
      g ≫ X.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k)))
        ∧ g.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k)) = e.base default}

/-- **Axiom-clean.** The `k`-rational identity-section point of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`:
the lift of the Picard scheme's identity section `MonObj.one` through the open
immersion `Pic⁰_{C/k} ↪ Pic_{C/k}`, i.e. the sibling's
`GroupScheme.identityComponentSection` specialised to `G = PicScheme C`
(transported along the definitional identification
`Pic0Scheme C = GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)`). This is the
`e`-witness of the Σ'-bundle in `tangentSpaceIso`. -/
noncomputable def identitySection {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
    Spec (.of k) ⟶ (Pic0Scheme C).left :=
  GroupScheme.identityComponentSection (PicScheme C)

/-- **Axiom-clean.** The identity-section point is a genuine section of the
structural morphism: `identitySection C ≫ (Pic0Scheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec k)`.
Transport of the sibling's `identityComponentSection_isSection`. -/
theorem identitySection_isSection {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
    identitySection C ≫ (Pic0Scheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) :=
  GroupScheme.identityComponentSection_isSection (PicScheme C)

/-- **Axiom-clean.** The Stacks 0B28 dictionary at the identity point: pointed
dual-number points of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` at `e` biject with `κ(e)`-linear functionals
on the cotangent space `m_e/m_e²`. Direct specialisation of
`overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual`
(`Picard/TangentSpaceIdentitySection.lean`) to `e = identitySection C`; the two
points `(identitySection C).base default` and
`(identitySection C).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)` are bridged by
`Subsingleton (Spec k)`, the same idiom `tangentSpaceCotangentDual` uses. -/
`ι : Pic⁰_{C/k} ↪ Pic_{C/k}` (an open immersion by the sibling's
`IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`), composition identifies the pointed
dual-number points at the identity section with those of the ambient Picard
scheme at its image — `Spec k[ε]` is a one-point scheme, so dual-number
points landing in the open subscheme lift uniquely
(`pointedDualNumberPointsEquivOfOpenImmersion`,
`Picard/Pic0TangentSpace.lean`). This lets the representability leg compute
`T_e Pic⁰` on `Pic_{C/k}` itself, where `picSharp`-representability applies. -/
theorem pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_picScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]

      pointedDualNumberPoints (Pic0Scheme C) (identitySection C) ≃
        pointedDualNumberPoints (PicScheme C) (identitySection C ≫ ι.left)) := by

    GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme (PicScheme C)
  haveI := hopen
  exact ⟨⟨f, pointedDualNumberPointsEquivOfOpenImmersion f (identitySection C)⟩⟩

/-- The **graded Hilbert function** of `F` at the fibre over `s : S`, relative
to the line bundle `L`:

`m ↦ dim_{κ(s)} Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})`,

the dimension over the residue field `κ(s)` of the global sections of the
`m`-th twist of the restriction `F_s` by `L_s` on the scheme-theoretic fibre
`X_s = π.fiber s`.  This is the graded Hilbert function of the section graded
module `M(X_s, F_s, L_s)` (`def:sectionGradedModule`); it uses only `H⁰`.
When the dimension is not finite, `Module.finrank` takes the junk value `0`.
Blueprint: the graded Hilbert function of `def:hilbert_polynomial`. -/
noncomputable def hilbertFunction (π : X ⟶ S) (L F : X.Modules) (s : S)
    (m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  letI := π.fiberSectionsModule s
    (Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow (π.fiberModule s F) (π.fiberModule s L) m)
  Module.finrank (S.residueField s)
    Γ(Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow (π.fiberModule s F) (π.fiberModule s L) m, ⊤)

/-- Two rational polynomials that agree at all sufficiently large natural
arguments are equal: the agreement set is infinite, so the difference has
infinitely many roots. -/
private lemma eq_of_eval_nat_eventually_eq {Φ Ψ : Polynomial ℚ} {N₁ N₂ : ℕ}
    {f : ℕ → ℚ} (h₁ : ∀ m : ℕ, N₁ < m → Φ.eval (m : ℚ) = f m)
    (h₂ : ∀ m : ℕ, N₂ < m → Ψ.eval (m : ℚ) = f m) : Φ = Ψ := by
  refine Polynomial.eq_of_infinite_eval_eq _ _ ?_
  apply ((Set.Ioi_infinite (max N₁ N₂)).image
    (Nat.cast_injective (R := ℚ)).injOn).mono
  rintro x ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩
  rw [Set.mem_Ioi, sup_lt_iff] at hn
  exact Set.mem_setOf_eq ▸ (h₁ n hn.1).trans (h₂ n hn.2).symm

/-- The **Hilbert polynomial** of a sheaf of modules `F` on `X` over `S` at
the fibre over `s ∈ S`, relative to the line bundle `L`
(`def:hilbert_polynomial`, [Nitsure] §1; cf. [Hartshorne] III.5.2): the
unique polynomial `Φ_{F,s} ∈ ℚ[λ]` that agrees, for all `m ≫ 0`, with the
graded Hilbert function

`m ↦ dim_{κ(s)} Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})`

of the fibre section module (`Scheme.hilbertFunction`), when such a
polynomial exists — and the junk value `0` otherwise.  Uniqueness holds
unconditionally (two polynomials agreeing at all large naturals are equal,
`Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eq_of_eventually`), so the extraction is canonical.

For proper `X_s`, ample `L_s` and coherent `F_s` the existence condition
holds (graded Hilbert–Serre; the `IsRatHilb`-conditional form is
`Scheme.existsUnique_hilbertPolynomial_of_isRatHilb`, and the remaining input
is the finite generation `lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`), and for `m ≫ 0` the
graded Hilbert function agrees with the Euler characteristic
`χ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` by Serre vanishing, so `Φ_{F,s}` is the classical
(Snapper) Hilbert polynomial — no numerical invariant is lost.  When `F` is
`S`-flat the function `s ↦ Φ_{F,s}` is locally constant on `S`. -/
noncomputable def hilbertPolynomial [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (π : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType π] (L F : X.Modules) (s : S) :
    Polynomial ℚ :=
  if h : ∃ Φ : Polynomial ℚ, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, N < m →
      Φ.eval (m : ℚ) = (hilbertFunction π L F s m : ℚ)
  then h.choose else 0

section HilbertPolynomialApi

variable [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (π : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType π]
variable (L F : X.Modules) (s : S)

/-- **Well-definedness of the Hilbert polynomial**: any polynomial that agrees
with the graded Hilbert function `m ↦ dim_{κ(s)} Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` for
all `m ≫ 0` *is* `hilbertPolynomial π L F s`.  This is the uniqueness clause
of `def:hilbert_polynomial`. -/
theorem hilbertPolynomial_eq_of_eventually {Φ : Polynomial ℚ} {N : ℕ}
    (hΦ : ∀ m : ℕ, N < m → Φ.eval (m : ℚ) = (hilbertFunction π L F s m : ℚ)) :
    hilbertPolynomial π L F s = Φ := by
  have h : ∃ Φ' : Polynomial ℚ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, N' < m →
      Φ'.eval (m : ℚ) = (hilbertFunction π L F s m : ℚ) := ⟨Φ, N, hΦ⟩
  rw [hilbertPolynomial, dif_pos h]
